data.title: Endava Receives Notice from NYSE Regarding Delayed Filing of Annual Report on Form 20-F
data.description:
Endava plc () (“Endava” or the “Company”) today announced that it received a notice from the New York Stock Exchange (the “NYSE”) on November 18, 2026 stating that the Company is not in compliance with the NYSE’s continued listing requirements under Section 802.01E of the NYSE Listed Company Manual as a result of the Company’s delay in filing its Annual Report on Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 (the “Annual Report”) with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”).

The notice has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of the Company’s securities on the NYSE subject to the Company’s compliance with other continued listing requirements.

As previously disclosed in a Form 12b-25 filed by the Company on November 3, 2026, the Company was unable, without unreasonable effort or expense, to file the Annual Report within the prescribed time period due to the internal investigation initiated by the Company’s Audit Committee into the accounting treatment of certain customer and supplier agreements. As a result of the investigation and the identification of separate accounting errors relating to revenue recognition, the Company is in the process of restating its previously reported financial results for fiscal 2026.

The Company’s preliminary estimate of the restatement’s impact on the Company’s previously reported fiscal 2026 financial results, its disclosure controls and procedures, and its internal control over financial reporting remains consistent with its press release issued on October 28, 2026. Endava expects adjustments to its fiscal 2026 revenue to be equivalent to approximately 2% – 4% of the Company’s fiscal 2025 revenue, it does not expect any adjustments to its fiscal 2025 results, and it does not expect a restatement of prior fiscal years or previous periods relating to those prior fiscal years. Management is currently in discussions with its lenders as it evaluates these matters and the potential impact on the Company’s revolving credit facility.

Under NYSE rules, Endava has a six-month period from the filing due date of November 17, 2026 to file the Annual Report with the SEC and regain compliance. The Company continues to work diligently with its advisors and auditors to file the Annual Report as soon as reasonably practicable and regain compliance with the NYSE’s continued listing requirements.

About Endava

Endava is a leading provider of next-generation technology services dedicated to enabling its clients to accelerate growth, tackle complex challenges and thrive in evolving markets. Endava embeds AI across the design and delivery of technology transformation, combining it with deep industry expertise to deliver measurable client outcomes with greater speed and precision. Central to Endava’s model is Dava.Flow™, its AI-native engagement lifecycle with governance, traceability and transparency built into the delivery process.

Endava’s clients span payments, insurance, banking and capital markets, technology, media, telecommunications, healthcare, mobility, retail and consumer goods and more. The Company’s team of more than 10,000 Endavans helps clients break new ground from locations in Europe, the Americas, Asia Pacific and the Middle East.

For more information, visit www.endava.com.

data.title: Diversified Energy Completes Birch Acquisition
data.description:
Diversified Energy Company (; ) ("Diversified" or the "Company") announces the close, on November 19, 2026, of its previously announced, accretive acquisition of Birch Permian Holdings, Inc. and certain affiliated companies (collectively, "Birch") from its former owners (the "Sellers") (the "Acquisition"). The Acquisition adds complementary operated producing properties and acreage positions in the Permian Basin (the "Assets"). In conjunction with the closing of the Acquisition, the Company closed on a $1,455 million asset backed securitization ("ABS XIV"), TCG Capital Markets L.L.C. served as Sole Structuring Agent and Sole Placement Agent on the financing. CIBC Capital Markets provided an LC Liquidity Facility to meet the liquidity reserve requirements.

Rusty Hutson, Jr., Chairman and CEO of Diversified, commented:

"We are excited to announce the closing of Birch, which delivers high-quality producing assets, durable cash flow, and a contiguous Permian Basin position. This highly accretive acquisition is exactly the type of transaction we focus on, where we can optimize the assets using our vertical integration and scale to meaningfully increase free cash flow for shareholders."

    -- 35% production increase to standalone Diversified(a)

    -- 70% liquids and 30% natural gas(a)

    interim cash flows and working capital liabilities; minimal DEC liquidity required at closing

    anticipated synergies
  • PDP reserves of 1,168 Bcfe(c) and PV-10 of $2.0 billion(d)

ABS Issuance Highlights

  • $1,455 million ABS notes structured as a master trust; Acquisition closing directly into the ABS eliminated the need for an acquisition bridge facility, reducing financing costs
  • Anchored by funds managed by The Carlyle Group "Carlyle", through the Company's strategic partnership with Carlyle, which was expanded to up to $10 billion of growth capital at the announcement of the Acquisition
  • The A tranche notes priced at a blended coupon of 6.84%, benefited by an investment-grade rating

data.title: Bausch + Lomb Reports Phase 2 Findings for BL1332 in Post-Surgical Ocular Pain
data.description:
Bausch + Lomb Corporation (NYSE/), a leading global eye health company dedicated to helping people see better to live better, today announced topline results from a Phase 2 study evaluating BL1332, a first-in-class topical TRPV1 antagonist, in patients experiencing pain following photorefractive keratectomy (PRK) surgery.

“What stands out from this study is the consistency of the findings,” said Yehia Hashad, MD, executive vice president, R&D and chief medical officer, Bausch + Lomb. “Both dose groups showed numerically greater pain relief than vehicle across all the pain measures we evaluated, more patients achieved complete pain relief following surgery and we observed evidence of faster corneal healing. These findings help define the clinical profile of BL1332 and will inform our discussions with the FDA on next steps, including potential Phase 3 planning.”

Ocular surface pain is a common and often debilitating condition that can occur following surgery and in association with a variety of ocular disorders. Despite its prevalence, there are currently no approved therapies specifically designed to target the underlying neurosensory pathways responsible for ocular surface pain.

BL1332 is a first-in-class topical TRPV1 antagonist designed to block a key receptor involved in ocular pain signaling. Unlike therapies that primarily address associated signs or symptoms, BL1332 is intended to directly modulate the biological pathways that drive ocular pain.

Study Design and Results

The randomized, double-masked, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group Phase 2 study evaluated BL1332 0.30% and BL1332 0.15% ophthalmic solution versus vehicle in 129 adults undergoing unilateral sequential PRK surgery for myopia. Participants were randomized 2:2:1 to BL1332 0.30%, BL1332 0.15% or vehicle and received treatment beginning immediately after surgery, with five doses administered over 24 hours while awake for three days and follow-up through Day 14.

The study was designed to identify an initial efficacy signal and characterize the clinical profile of BL1332 in post-surgical patients.

The study did not meet its primary endpoint of demonstrating a statistically significant improvement versus vehicle in the sum of pain intensity differences (SPID) over 24 hours. The least-squares mean difference versus vehicle was -11.5 for BL1332 0.30% and -9.0 for BL1332 0.15%, with negative values favoring BL1332 indicating greater pain relief.

Both BL1332 dose groups demonstrated numerically greater pain relief than vehicle across every SPID analysis conducted, including the primary endpoint, secondary endpoints and exploratory analyses through 72 hours after surgery. Consistent directional improvement was observed across all prespecified pain assessment windows.

For the secondary endpoint measuring pain reduction during the first six hours after surgery, the 0.30% dose demonstrated a nominally significant reduction versus vehicle.

Exploratory Findings

Additional exploratory analyses provided further insight into the clinical profile of BL1332.

At every assessment between six and 12 hours after surgery, a greater proportion of patients receiving either BL1332 dose reported complete pain relief compared with vehicle. At six hours following surgery, complete pain relief was reported by 14.0% and 14.6% of patients receiving BL1332 0.30% and 0.15%, respectively, compared with 3.7% of patients receiving vehicle.

In an anterior segment OCT subset, patients treated with either BL1332 dose demonstrated greater central corneal epithelial thickness at Day 3 compared with vehicle. These findings were consistent with faster healing of the corneal surface following surgery and support further evaluation in future studies.

Safety

BL1332 was well tolerated.

Treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 6.0% of patients receiving BL1332 0.30%, 13.7% of patients receiving BL1332 0.15% and 14.8% of patients receiving vehicle. There were no treatment-related adverse events, serious adverse events or discontinuations due to adverse events.

The safety profile was considered acceptable, with no new safety signals identified.

Path Forward

Bausch + Lomb is completing its analysis of the full dataset and expects to discuss the findings with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

The company is evaluating study designs, endpoints and patient populations that best align with the clinical profile observed in this study. These findings, together with results from a previously reported Phase 1b study of BL1332 in participants with capsaicin-induced pain, will help shape discussions with the FDA and the program's future development.

data.description:

Future dividend declarations will be made at the discretion of the Assurant Board of Directors and will depend on various factors, including the company’s earnings, financial condition, capital requirements, subsidiaries’ payments of dividends to the company, future prospects, regulatory restrictions and other considerations.

data.title: Why Walmart is making a bigger bet on fast-food delivery
data.description:
By Bill Peters

The retail giant says around 90% of spending at fast-food chains occurs within a few miles from a Walmart

Walmart reported quarterly earnings on Thursday.

As Walmart expands its delivery service, it also wants to handle more of your takeout orders.

During its quarterly earnings call on Thursday, the big-box chain (WMT) said it was using its vast online-ordering infrastructure to deliver more meals from fast-food restaurants to customers' homes, alongside groceries and other items. Walmart executives said chains like Papa John's (PZZA) were already on board and consumer interest was strong.

"If you think about it from our standpoint, it helps us capture more meal occasions, which then drives traffic as well as increased frequency to our site and to our app," David Guggina, the CEO of Walmart U.S., said during the call, according to an AlphaSense transcript.

"About 90% of QSR spend happens within a few miles of a Walmart," he noted, referring to quick-service restaurants. "So in Q3, we leaned in. We've now expanded to over 2,700 restaurant locations. We added Dunkin' this past quarter, we expanded Subway and we announced our partnership with Papa John's."

Guggina added that those restaurant deliveries helped "keep our drivers engaged" and strengthened the retailer's last-mile network, or the final stretch of an item's journey before it arrives at a customer's doorstep. The company said it was rapidly scaling the service and thinking of other ways to expand its delivery capabilities.

Walmart in June began allowing customers in some areas to order items from Subway through the Walmart app or the retailer's website, either on its own or with an order for other items via Walmart Express. The sandwich chain is already the biggest in-store restaurant at Walmart, following a partnership that started in 2004.

"The future of retail is about bringing more of customers' everyday needs into a single, seamless experience," Tracy Poulliot, executive vice president of e-commerce and marketing at Walmart U.S., said in a press release in June.

Apps like Instacart (CART) already handle deliveries from retailers like Walmart and Costco Wholesale (COST). Doordash (DASH), which wants to combine with Instacart, delivers from restaurants as well as retailers. Over the years, the delivery-app industry has consolidated and platforms have increasingly offered similar services to compete.

Walmart's quarterly results on Thursday squeaked past Wall Street's estimates, and the company raised its full-year earnings and same-store sales outlook. During the earnings call, Walmart CEO John Furner said that e-commerce drove the company's sales gains during its third quarter, which ran through October. The company's third-quarter e-commerce sales rose 17%.

Shares of Walmart were down 1.3% on Thursday. However, the stock was up 12.8% so far this year. Shares were trading at nearly $126, off highs of more than $130 reached earlier this year.

Furner on Thursday described Walmart's customers as "stable" and "resilient" as they navigate rising costs of living that have hit its lower-income shoppers harder. Analysts have said that Walmart's delivery ecosystem, and its efforts to make it faster, have helped it attract wealthier customers who have turned to the retailer in search of lower prices.

"We no longer see stores and e-commerce as separate, but connected parts of an integrated ecosystem," Furner said on Thursday's call. "We can now reach 96% of U.S. households in less than three hours, and 60% in less than 30 minutes."

-Bill Peters

data.title: Boston Beer Taps Operating Chief Hodges to Be Next CEO
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Boston Beer Co. named Chief Operating Officer Phil Hodges as its new chief executive.

Hodges will succeed founder Jim Koch, who is stepping down after returning to the helm last year.

Koch returned as chief executive in August 2025 after Michael Spillane departed, citing personal reasons. Koch held the role from the company's founding in 1984 through 2001. He will continue as executive chair of the board and serve as a resource to Hodges on long-term strategy, culture and industry relationships, the company said.

Hodges has been operating chief since October 2025. Before that, he was chief supply chain officer starting in May 2023, after joining the company as a supply chain consultant in 2022.

He has helped Boston Beer improve service levels, brewery production, procurement efficiency and inventory management, the company said. He also helped the company expand its gross margins.

Hodges brings 30 years of experience in the consumer packaged goods industry, and previously worked at Carlsberg, Kraft Foods International and Mondelez International.

When Koch rejoined as chief executive last year, he said there were multiple people within the company who would be good candidates to lead, but none were ready yet.

Hodges is stepping into the role at a difficult time for the industry, as consumers are buying less beer and some are quitting drinking altogether. In October, Boston Beer reported lower profit and revenue during its third quarter, as beer demand continued to fall.

"The demand environment remains challenging, and we are prioritizing actions within our control to strengthen our business and improve market share trends," Koch said in October.

data.title: Grandstand Reports Third Quarter Results, Updates 2026 Guidance and Initiates Review of Strategic Alternatives
data.description:
Grandstand Limited () (the “Company” or "Grandstand"), the intelligence layer powering informed decisions for consumers and partners across sports, gaming and entertainment, today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. In addition, the Company provided updated 2026 full year guidance and announced that its Board of Directors has initiated a review of strategic alternatives to maximize shareholder value.

Kevin McCrystle, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of Grandstand Limited, commented, "Revenue of $40.2 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $10.0 million in the third quarter rose by 7% and 30%, respectively, on a quarterly sequential basis. Adjusted EBITDA margins improved from 20% to 25% sequentially, and we converted 80% of Adjusted EBITDA to Adjusted Free Cash Flow. Data revenue grew 17% year over year, while marketing revenue declined slightly year-over-year but grew contribution margin compared to Q2 2026.

“While we saw significant growth and margin expansion quarter-over-quarter, the rate of growth was lower than forecasted, leading to lower-than-expected revenue and Adjusted EBITDA, and, as a result, we are adjusting our 2026 full year guidance. Our partner-facing businesses, including enterprise data and Grandstand partners, continue to perform well and grow at attractive rates, but our consumer brands are performing below their potential. We are taking decisive action to deliver accelerated growth and expanded margins in 2027 through continued focus on operational transformation, the benefits of our diversified marketing business, streamlined portfolio management of brand assets, the ramp of Rollcard and disciplined cost control.”

“Our platform of technologies and brands remain highly profitable and cash generative, and we believe the Company's current market valuation does not reflect the strength of the business and its cash flow generation. With that in mind, the Board has initiated a review of strategic alternatives to maximize value for shareholders,” said McCrystle.

Elias Mark, Chief Financial Officer of Grandstand Limited, added, “We are on track to generate almost $30 million in Adjusted Free Cash Flow this year despite currently performing below our expectations, illustrating the under-appreciated attractive economics of our business model. We expect that the quarterly sequential improvement in our Adjusted EBITDA margins in the second half of this year will carry forward into 2027, with consistently high cash conversion, resulting in healthy growth in Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted Free Cash Flow that will allow us to continue to de-lever our balance sheet.”

Strategic Review Process

Grandstand's Board of Directors has initiated a review of strategic alternatives to maximize shareholder value, and the Company has engaged Jefferies as its financial advisor in connection with this review. During this review process, the Company expects to evaluate a broad range of strategic alternatives including the refinancing of its outstanding debt with the aim of extending its maturity profile and providing the Company with additional financial flexibility. The Board and management team remain fully committed to acting in the best interests of the Company and its shareholders, and management remains focused on executing the Company’s business plan and serving its partners throughout the review.

The Company has not set a timetable for the conclusion of its evaluation, nor has it made any decisions related to its review of any potential actions at this time. Grandstand does not intend to disclose further developments with respect to the review unless and until the Board approves a specific course of action or otherwise determines that further disclosure is appropriate or required. There can be no assurances as to the outcome or the timing of such review, or whether any particular action may be pursued or consummated.

Disaggregated Revenue

Revenue is disaggregated based on how the nature, amount, timing and uncertainty of the revenue and cash flows are affected by economic factors.

Marketing

Performance marketing. Performance marketing revenue consists of (i) Cost Per Acquisition (“CPA”) revenue from arrangements where we are paid exclusively by a single cash payment for each referred player, (ii) revenue share arrangements where we are paid exclusively by a share of the customer’s net gambling revenue ("NGR") from the referred players, (iii) hybrid revenue from arrangements where we are paid by both a CPA commission and a revenue share commission from the referred players and (iv) ticketing revenue from fees and commissions from ticket reservations for recreational and leisure events.

Within performance marketing arrangements, the Company considers each referred player and each ticket reservation to represent a separate performance obligation.

The performance obligation of referral arrangements is satisfied at the point in time when the referral is accepted by the relevant online gambling operator. Revenue share fees for each referred player are considered variable consideration and are only recognized to the extent it is probable that no significant reversal of cumulative revenue recognized for the referral will occur when the ultimate fees are known.

CPA fees for each referred player are recognized when earned upon acceptance of the referral by the online gambling operator.

Fees generated by each customer during a particular month are typically paid to us within 30-45 days after the invoice date.

The Company acts as an agent in ticketing arrangements as it does not control the underlying event. The revenue is recognized on a net basis, calculated as the proceeds collected from a customer less the cost of the ticket sold. Ticketing revenue is recognized at a point in time when the sale is made as the Company’s performance obligation is to facilitate and process the transaction and issue the ticket.

Advertising and other. Advertising, media and other revenue includes revenue from arrangements not based on the referred players and includes advertising on our platform and onboarding fees. Revenue is recognized on a straight-line basis over the term of the contract.

Data

Subscription. Data revenue consists of consumer and enterprise subscription revenue from data, data analytics and data syndication services. For subscription revenue, the Company considers each subscription to be a separate performance obligation. The Company satisfies its performance obligation, and revenue from these services is recognized, on a straight-line basis over the subscription period. The Company records deferred revenue upon execution of subscriptions when the subscription plan requires upfront payment.

Non-IFRS Financial Measures

Management uses both IFRS and non-IFRS financial measures in analyzing and assessing the overall performance of the business and for making operational decisions.

Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted Net Income Per Share

Adjusted net income is a non-IFRS financial measure defined as net income attributable to shareholders adjusted to exclude the effect of non-recurring items, significant non-cash items, unwinding of deferred consideration, gain on early settlement of deferred consideration, employees’ bonuses related to acquisition, deferred revenue fair value adjustment, share-based payment and related expense, amortization expenses related to acquired businesses and assets, restructuring costs and other items that our board of directors believes do not reflect the underlying performance of the business, including acquisition related expenses, such as acquisition related costs and bonuses.

Adjusted net income per diluted share is a non-IFRS financial measure defined as Adjusted net income attributable to shareholders divided by the diluted weighted average number of ordinary shares outstanding.

We believe Adjusted net income and Adjusted net income per diluted share are useful to our management as a measure of comparative performance from period to period as these measures remove gain on early settlement of deferred consideration, the unwinding of deferred consideration, employees’ bonuses related to acquisition, deferred revenue fair value adjustment, share-based payment and related expense, restructuring costs and other expenses associated with our restructuring, acquisition related costs, amortization expenses related to acquired businesses and assets, and all other items associated with our acquisitions, during the limited period where these items are incurred. The unwinding of deferred consideration for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 is associated with the unwinding of the discount applied to the valuation of the deferred consideration for the OddsJam Acquisition during the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

While we use Adjusted net income and Adjusted net income per share as tools to enhance our understanding of certain aspects of our financial performance, we do not believe that Adjusted net income and Adjusted net income per share are substitutes for, or superior to, the information provided by IFRS results. As such, the presentation of Adjusted net income and Adjusted net income per share is not intended to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for any measure prepared in accordance with IFRS. The primary limitations associated with the use of Adjusted net income and Adjusted net income per share as compared to IFRS results are that Adjusted net income and Adjusted net income per share as we define them may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other companies in our industry and that Adjusted net income and Adjusted net income per share may exclude financial information that some investors may consider important in evaluating our performance.

data.title: Elastic Reports Second Quarter Fiscal 2027 Financial Results
data.description:
Elastic () announced financial results for its second quarter of fiscal 2027 ended October 31, 2026.

Second Quarter Fiscal 2027 Financial Highlights

  • Total revenue was $496 million, an increase of 17% year-over-year, as reported and on a constant currency basis

  • Total subscription revenue was $465 million, an increase of 17% year-over-year, as reported and on a constant currency basis

  • Sales-led subscription revenue (calculated as subscription revenue excluding Monthly Elastic Cloud) was $415 million, an increase of 19% year-over-year, as reported and on a constant currency basis

  • Current remaining performance obligations were $1.157 billion, an increase of 19% year-over-year, or 20% on a constant currency basis

  • Remaining performance obligations were $1.858 billion, an increase of 23% year-over-year, or 24% on a constant currency basis

  • GAAP operating income was $22 million; GAAP operating margin was 4.4%; GAAP diluted earnings per share was $0.00

  • Non-GAAP operating income was $110 million; non-GAAP operating margin was 22.2%; non-GAAP diluted earnings per share was $0.94

  • Operating cash flow and adjusted free cash flow were $44 million

  • Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $1.423 billion as of October 31, 2026

“Elastic delivered another strong quarter, beating guidance across all key metrics,” said Ash Kulkarni, CEO of Elastic. “In Q2, we accelerated our AI innovation with new capabilities such as AlertZero, Elastic® nightshift, and Elastic Context Engine, and I’m personally very excited about our agreement to acquire HoneyHive, which will allow us to expand our business in the area of agent observability and evaluations. We are also pleased with the continued growth of our $1M+ customer cohort, similar to the solid net additions we saw during the first quarter. Our strong results reflect expanding customer adoption and position us well to continue our strong execution in the back half of fiscal 2027.”

Second Quarter Fiscal 2027 Key Metrics and Recent Business Highlights

Key Customer Metrics

  • Total customer count with Annual Contract Value (ACV) greater than $100,000 was over 1,830 compared to over 1,800 in Q1 FY27, and over 1,600 in Q2 FY26

  • Net Expansion Rate was approximately 111%

Product Innovations and Updates

  • Unveiled Elastic© nightshift AI SRE in private preview, an AI agent built into Elastic Observability that continuously detects and investigates issues across the entire stack, delivering evidence-backed root cause analysis and recommended fixes

  • Announced AlertZero in technical preview, a team of specialized AI agents built into Elastic Security to automate alert triage, threat hunting, investigation, detection tuning and forensic analysis, helping security teams accelerate response to evolving cyber threats

  • Announced a new optimized serverless offering for Elasticsearch Vector Database for large-scale vector search and AI applications, enabling developers to deploy vector search in minutes and scale affordably to hundreds of billions of vectors

  • Made cross-project search generally available for Elastic Cloud Serverless, enabling customers to query data across projects, regions, and cloud providers without moving or duplicating data

  • Released jina-ocr-v1, an end-to-end optical character recognition model that converts complex documents, including tables, handwriting, and mathematical notation into structured, machine-readable text across more than 100 languages

  • Announced plans to integrate OpenAI GPT cyber models into Elastic Security, bringing specialized cyber reasoning capabilities into existing security workflows to accelerate threat investigation and remediation

  • Organizations now face threats that move at AI-speed. We’re announcing that we have joined Anthropic’s Cyber Verification Program to give our security teams an advantage against this new attack surface.

Other Business Highlights

  • Appointed Julia Liuson, former president of Microsoft's Developer Division, to Elastic's board of directors, bringing more than three decades of leadership experience across AI, developer platforms, and enterprise technology

  • Recognized as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Enterprise AI Search, positioned highest for Ability to Execute and furthest for Completeness of Vision

  • Achieved the only perfect protection score in the 2026 AV-Comparatives Endpoint Prevention and Response Test, stopping all 50 attack scenarios at the first phase of compromise with zero false positives

  • Announced an agreement to acquire HoneyHive, Inc., an emerging leader in agent observability and evaluation, to help our customers observe, evaluate, and trust the agents they run in production

  • Announced a multi-year partnership with Audi Revolut F1® Team, building on the team's existing use of Elastic's search and observability technology to support its engineering software operations

Share Repurchase Program

In October 2025, Elastic announced a share repurchase program pursuant to which the Company may repurchase up to $500 million of the Company’s outstanding ordinary shares. As part of this program, during the second quarter of fiscal 2027, Elastic repurchased approximately 0.6 million ordinary shares at an average price per share of $86.31 on the open market, representing an aggregate value of approximately $55 million. The Board has authorized a new $500 million repurchase program (including approximately $45 million remaining availability under the existing program).

Financial Outlook

During our last guidance, we anticipated FX rates of 1.17 against the Euro and 1.36 against the Pound. The dollar has subsequently strengthened to 1.09 against the Euro, and 1.31 against the Pound. The stronger dollar will result in a total revenue headwind of $4.5 million in Q3, and $5.0 million in Q4, a total of $9.5 million of currency-related headwind in the second half of fiscal 2027.

Against this backdrop, the Company is providing the following guidance:

For the third quarter of fiscal 2027 (ending January 31, 2027):

  • Total revenue is expected to be between $507.5 million and $508.5 million, representing 12.9% year-over-year growth at the midpoint (13.9% year-over-year constant currency growth at the midpoint). This guidance incorporates a $4.5 million FX headwind to the midpoint.

  • Sales-led subscription revenue is expected to be between $432.0 million and $433.0 million, representing 15.1% year-over-year growth at the midpoint (16.2% year-over-year constant currency growth at the midpoint). This guidance incorporates a $4.0 million FX headwind to the midpoint.

  • GAAP operating margin is expected to be positive

  • Non-GAAP operating margin is expected to be approximately 21.0%

  • Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share is expected to be between $0.90 and $0.92, assuming between 108.5 million and 109.5 million diluted weighted average ordinary shares outstanding

For fiscal 2027 (ending April 30, 2027):

  • Total revenue is expected to be between $2.000 billion and $2.008 billion, representing 15.2% year-over-year growth at the midpoint (15.9% year-over-year constant currency growth at the midpoint). This guidance incorporates a $9.5 million FX headwind to the midpoint.

  • Sales-led subscription revenue is expected to be between $1.682 billion and $1.690 billion, representing 17.2% year-over-year growth at the midpoint (18.0% year-over-year constant currency growth at the midpoint). This guidance incorporates a $9.0 million FX headwind to the midpoint.

  • GAAP operating margin is expected to be positive

  • Non-GAAP operating margin is expected to be approximately 19.5%

  • Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share is expected to be between $3.35 and $3.41, assuming between 108.0 million and 109.0 million diluted weighted average ordinary shares outstanding

  • Adjusted free cash flow margin is expected to be approximately 21.5%, excluding any acquisitions or other one-time charges

The diluted weighted average ordinary shares outstanding reflect only share buybacks completed as of October 31, 2026.

The midpoint of the guidance range assumes the following exchange rates, among others: 1 Euro = 1.09 US Dollars; and 1 Great British Pound = 1.31 US Dollars.

Conference Call and Webcast

Statement Regarding Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures

In addition to our results determined in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”), we believe the non-GAAP measures discussed below are useful in evaluating our operating performance. We use these non-GAAP financial measures to evaluate our ongoing operations and for internal planning and forecasting purposes. We believe that non-GAAP financial information, when taken collectively, may be helpful to investors because it provides consistency and comparability with past financial performance. However, non-GAAP financial information is presented for supplemental informational purposes only, has limitations as an analytical tool and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for financial information presented in accordance with GAAP. In addition, other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate similarly-titled non-GAAP measures differently or may use other measures to evaluate their performance, all of which could reduce the usefulness of our non-GAAP financial measures as tools for comparison. Investors are cautioned that there are a number of limitations associated with the use of non-GAAP financial measures and key metrics as analytical tools. Investors are encouraged to review the differences between GAAP financial measures and the corresponding non-GAAP financial measures, and not to rely on any single financial measure to evaluate our business and financial results.

Reconciliations of historical GAAP financial measures to their respective historical non-GAAP financial measures are included below. In relation to constant currency non-GAAP financial measures, the only reconciling item between GAAP financial measures and non-GAAP financial measures is the effect of foreign currency rate fluctuations. Further details on how we calculate such effects can be found in the definition of “Constant Currency” below.

Sales-led Subscription Revenue

Sales-led subscription revenue is a non-GAAP financial measure that we calculate as total subscription revenue excluding Monthly Elastic Cloud. We believe sales-led subscription revenue provides management and our investors with a consistent metric with which to measure the health of our business.

Non-GAAP Gross Profit and Non-GAAP Gross Margin

We define non-GAAP gross profit and non-GAAP gross margin as GAAP gross profit and GAAP gross margin, respectively, excluding stock-based compensation expense and related employer taxes, and amortization of acquired intangible assets. We believe non-GAAP gross profit and non-GAAP gross margin provide our management and investors consistency and comparability with our past financial performance and facilitate period-to-period comparisons of operations, as these metrics generally eliminate the effects of certain variables from period to period for reasons unrelated to overall operating performance.

Non-GAAP Operating Income and Non-GAAP Operating Margin

We define non-GAAP operating income and non-GAAP operating margin as GAAP operating income/(loss) and GAAP operating margin, respectively, excluding stock-based compensation expense and related employer taxes, amortization of acquired intangible assets, acquisition-related expenses, and restructuring and other related charges. We believe non-GAAP operating income and non-GAAP operating margin provide our management and investors consistency and comparability with our past financial performance and facilitate period-to-period comparisons of operations, as these metrics generally eliminate the effects of certain variables from period to period for reasons unrelated to overall operating performance.

Non-GAAP Net Income and Non-GAAP Earnings Per Share

We define non-GAAP net income as GAAP income/(loss), excluding stock-based compensation expense and related employer taxes, amortization of acquired intangible assets, acquisition-related expenses, restructuring and other related charges, and the income tax benefit from the release of any valuation allowance against deferred tax assets. Additionally, non-GAAP net income and non-GAAP earnings per share are adjusted for an assumed provision for income taxes based on a projected non-GAAP annual effective tax rate in fiscal 2027 and 2026 of 12% and 13%, respectively. We define non-GAAP earnings per share, basic, as non-GAAP net income divided by weighted average shares outstanding and non-GAAP earnings per share, diluted, as non-GAAP net income divided by weighted average diluted shares outstanding, which includes the potentially dilutive effect of the Company’s employee equity incentive plan awards. We believe non-GAAP earnings per share provides our management and investors consistency and comparability with our past financial performance and facilitates period-to-period comparisons of operations, as this metric generally eliminates the effects of certain variables from period to period for reasons unrelated to overall operating performance.

Adjusted Free Cash Flow and Adjusted Free Cash Flow Margin

Adjusted free cash flow is a non-GAAP financial measure that we define as net cash provided by operating activities adjusted for cash paid for interest on long-term debt less cash used for investing activities for purchases of property and equipment. Adjusted free cash flow margin is calculated as adjusted free cash flow divided by total revenue. Adjusted free cash flow does not represent residual cash flow available for discretionary expenditures since, among other things, we have mandatory debt service requirements.

Constant Currency

We compare the percent change in certain results from one period to another period using constant currency information to provide a framework for assessing how our business performed excluding the effect of foreign currency rate fluctuations. In presenting this information, current and comparative prior period results are converted into United States dollars at the exchange rates in effect on the last day of our prior fiscal year, rather than the actual exchange rates in effect during the respective periods.
